messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the continuous-batching RFC – we need to pick a rollout path. I sketched three approaches (incremental adapter, conservative swap, and hybrid fastpath) + testing checklist. Wanted opinions before I turn this into a concrete PR.

devin: Thx Maya. Can you paste the short pros/cons for each?

maya: Sure – tl;dr: incremental adapter = least risky but more runtime overhead; conservative swap = clean but big blast radius; hybrid = best perf/cost but trickiest to test.

maya: incremental adapter details:
- keep current admission surface, add adapter that coalesces windows into new batching runtime
- adapter exposes same enqueue/dequeue contracts, does preflight admission hooks
- advantage: small API churn, can A/B per-pool
- downside: extra copy/handshake path and slight CPU in fastpath

sasha: For the adapter path: how do we handle KV cache affinity? that's where most regressions happen.

maya: Good call. Plan is adapter to signal kvcache pins on batch boundaries. Adapter will add a "pin_hint" header to the existing request envelope so kvcache can prefer sticky placements. No API change to external callers.

devin: conservative swap details?

maya: conservative swap:
- replace current coalescer with new runtime behind a feature flag at node/pool level
- migrate tenants by moving routing rules; minimal runtime branching
- advantage: simpler codepaths in hot path, better perf
- downside: migration requires coordinated routing changes and fallback plans if latency regresses

jen: Hybrid fastpath: sounds appealing but operationally scary. What's the fallback story if a hybrid batch path fails mid-request?

maya: hybrid fastpath:
- keep existing path as fallback; route small requests to fastpath micro-window aggregator and large ones to legacy path, with a runtime probe to decide placement
- on failure, adapter short-circuits to legacy with idempotency token and replay safety
- requires idempotency headers + short-lived reservation token for in-flight KV state

alex: Where does admission live in hybrid? we can't have two different credit models out of sync.

maya: Admission stays centralized in scheduler service. Adapter reports expected window sizes and token costs. Scheduler keeps a single ledger and issues soft-credits for fastpath; hard credits for legacy. We'll need a reconciliation job to surface drift.

sasha: Metrics we must track (minimal set):
- per-path P50/P95/P99 latency
- enqueue->dispatch time histogram
- kvcache miss/hit by path
- batch size distribution and packing efficiency
- failed-fallback rate and replay count

devin: Agree. Also add per-tenant token accounting deltas so finance can see cost impact during canary.

jen: Testing checklist I mentioned?
maya: wrote a dev checklist:
1) unit tests for adapter handshake and pin_hint propagation
2) integration tests with kvcache simulation (hot cache vs cold cache)
3) stress test: multi-tenant load with synthetic shard skew
4) chaos: kill aggregator mid-batch and assert fallback + no data loss
5) long-tail perf test: 24h run with slow tail injection
6) telemetry: build dashboards and alert thresholds for fallback rate > 0.5%

alex: Can we reuse the existing canary infra? I want progressive ramp: 1 pool -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> full. Also tombstone route if we exceed fallback threshold.

maya: Yes, use canary infra + rollout-operator. We'll add an automated rollback hook if latency regressions exceed SLO or fallback rate > threshold.

sasha: Implementation concerns: the adapter introduces a new RPC on enqueue. Do we version the broker API or piggyback on metadata?

maya: Piggyback on metadata for now (kinda ugly) to avoid version hell. We'll make it v2 in next major when we do broader refactors. Metadata keys: x-batch-window, x-pin-hint, x-reservation-token. Example envelope: 

```
{
  "meta": { "x-batch-window": "16ms", "x-pin-hint": "k:v:1234", "x-reservation-token": "rt_..." },
  "payload": { ... }
}
```

devin: Can we get away with binary flags to minimize overhead? JSON meta is fine for prototyping but we should keep wire cost low.

maya: Good point – adapter will serialize metadata as compact proto on the internal path, logs/samples will expand to JSON for observability.

jen: Security: reservation tokens need short TTL and must be signed by the scheduler. Add KMS signing to the plan.

alex: Also consider a lease revocation path if kvcache migration forces eviction. Need a signal to preempt pinned KV gently.

sasha: Rollout timeline proposal?

maya: Draft timeline (rough):
- week 1: adapter prototype + unit tests
- week 2: internal proto + integration with kvcache mock
- week 3: perf tuning + small pool canary (non-prod)
- week 4: prod canary 5% -> 25% with dashboards live
- week 5: evaluate, decide hybrid vs swap full cutover

devin: Sounds aggressive but doable if we parallelize. We should reserve a rollback window and coordinate oncall.

jen: Also add a DB migration if we add any scheduler ledger columns. Keep migrations additive and backward compatible.

alex: One more item: cost modeling. We need a before/after per-token CPU estimate for finance signoff. The adapter costs are CPU + memory for extra buffers; swap reduces CPU but may raise ops complexity.

maya: I'll draft a short cost model: adapter adds ~3-5% CPU on p99 loads, swap reduces token CPU by ~8-12% in early tests. Will attach numbers to the PR.

devin: OK next steps: Maya turns this into a design PR with the checklist, proto sketch, and canary plan. I'll volunteer to own the canary run. Sasha will own kvcache integration tests. Jen will scope the security/KMS bits. Alex will work on cost modeling and migration notes.

maya: Thanks all. I'll open PR tomorrow and ping this thread. Ping if you want to pair on tests. :rocket:

infra-bot: Deploy-canary: scheduled 2026-05-03T04:00:00Z for pool dev-agg-01 (dry-run)

devin: nice, thanks infra-bot

jen: small nit – add a short paragraph on observability ownership in the PR (who monitors dashboards during canary).

maya: Good call, added to my TODO.

alex: sgtm.

sasha: 👍

maya: Closing loop — PR is up: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/842 (will add the proto in next commit)
